title: District Environment Plan (DEP) Snapshot
note: District Environment Plans are prepared at the district level and are not river-basin-specific: the figures below cover each district's full extent, of which only a share drains to the Kabini (Mysuru 54.6%, Chamarajanagara 22.4%, Kodagu 4.1%, computed against the KWRIS C2 sub-basin polygon). This is a district-grain first pass; Arkavathi-style per-ULB depth for every theme is a later phase.

items.heading: Who executes the plan
items.body: The NGT's compliance framework puts the District Magistrate in charge: DEP action plans are to be executed with progress on targets reviewed at least once a month, and states must consolidate their DEPs into a State Environment Plan published on the state website.

source.source: NGT order 05.07.2021 in OA 360/2018 (directions d and e)
source.says: “The District Magistrates may accordingly execute the action plans by reviewing the progress on various targets at least once in a month.”
source.citation: CPCB status report on DEP preparation before the NGT, OA 360/2018, p.5

items.heading: What the plans must cover
items.body: Per the NGT's scope in OA 360/2018, every DEP covers 7 thematic areas: waste management (solid, plastic, C&D, biomedical, hazardous, e-waste), water quality, domestic sewage, industrial wastewater, air quality, mining activity and noise pollution. The tabs above follow that structure.

gaps: No updated edition of any of the three districts' DEPs has been published since 2021/2022 - progress against the plans' own timelines (most fall due 2021-2023) is not visible in the public domain.
If District Magistrates hold the mandated monthly reviews, no known public record of their minutes or outcomes exists.
No known public copy of Karnataka's consolidated State Environment Plan, required by direction (e) to be uploaded on the state website.

The Chamarajanagar DEP never mentions the Kabini river at all - its water chapters frame the district entirely around the Cauvery, Suvarnavathi and Palar, although 22.4% of the district lies in the Kabini sub-basin.

districts.name: Mysuru

dep.label: Revised District Environmental Plan of Mysuru District (May 2022, 70 pp)

counts.label: Town Municipal Councils (TMC)
counts.value: 5 - KR Nagar, Periyapatna, HD Kote, TN Pura, Bannur

districts.countsNote: The Kabini-side ULBs are Nanjangud CMC, TN Pura TMC, HD Kote TMC and Sargur TP - their cards below carry the plan's ULB-wise sewage and waste figures. The plan itself lists the Nanjangud-Hejjige reach among the district's polluted river stretches (p.48).
conflicts: The plan states the district's industrial wastewater as 25.6746 MLD in the water-quality chapter (p.49) but 19.681862 MLD in the industrial-wastewater chapter (p.62).

The domestic-sewage chapter reports 105.34 MLD of untreated or partially treated sewage reaching water bodies (p.59), while its own action plan concludes 'The existing STP is adequate to treat the generated sewage' (p.61).
The T. Narasipura STP is listed as an existing 5.5 MLD plant on p.57 and again in the gap table on p.60, but the treatment-capacity table on p.59 shows TN Pura at 0 MLD.

districtThemes.summary: ULB-wise inventory across the corporation and 8 towns: 254 urban wards of which 248 report 100% source segregation; Gram Panchayat quantities are theoretical (200 g/head/day).

metrics.label: Nanjangud CMC / TN Pura TMC / HD Kote TMC / Sargur TP

openActions: Action plan to achieve 100% segregation at source; awareness programmes and incentives - Urban Local Bodies - 31-03-2023

districtThemes.summary: The plan inventories the Cauvery (144.51 km in-district), 17 drains meeting rivers and 745 lakes, and names three polluted river stretches including Nanjangud to Hejjige on the Kabini; its own gap analysis is that no district environmental monitoring cell exists and lake water quality is not monitored at all.

metrics.label: Polluted river stretches named by the plan
metrics.value: Mysuru Bannur Road Bridge; Hunsur to Kattemalavadi; Nanjungud to Hejjige

metrics.label: Lake water quality monitoring
metrics.value: Not carried out; frequency not fixed (plan's own gap)

metrics.label: Groundwater observation borewells
metrics.value: 59, monitored monthly for levels; quality twice yearly

metrics.label: GEC 2017 taluk categorisation
metrics.value: Mysuru taluk semi-critical; remaining 6 taluks safe

openActions: Constitute an environmental monitoring cell and inventorise drains, canals, rivers, groundwater, ponds and lakes - Minor Irrigation Dept + MUDA + Groundwater Authority + CNNL + Zilla Panchayat + KSPCB - 31-03-2023
Increase KSPCB sampling points along the monitored river stretches - KSPCB - 31-03-2023
Lake owners (ULBs / Gram / Taluk panchayats) to monitor lake water quality per CPCB frequency and report quarterly - 31-03-2023
ULBs to identify wastewater-carrying drains joining water bodies and plug them; drain-end treatment and bar meshes - ULBs - 31-03-2022

districtThemes.summary: District sewage is 206.74 MLD (of which Mysuru city 180) against 199.41 MLD of installed STP capacity; the plan's own flow table shows 17.48 MLD of treated sewage reaching rivers while 105.34 MLD flows untreated or partially treated and 92.2 MLD reaches lakes. Three towns still need treatment: Periyapatna (4.2 MLD STP under construction), HD Kote (FSTP approved only) and Sargur (nothing).

metrics.label: Towns needing STPs
metrics.value: 3 - Periyapatna (4.2 MLD under construction), HD Kote (FSTP approved), Sargur (none)

openActions: Complete UGD connections to close the missing links bypassing STPs - LBs + KUWS&DB + Zilla Panchayat - 31-03-2023
DPR for channelization and interception of all drains (excluding industrial) for treatment through upcoming STPs - 31-03-2023
Install web cams and OCEMS in STPs - 31-03-2023
Formulate an action plan for long-term use of treated STP water - 31-03-2023

districtThemes.summary: By the KSPCB Regional Office F-register (31-08-2021) the district has 1,096 categorised industries of which 931 discharge wastewater; the plan reports the full 19.68 MLD as treated in-house, no CETP in the district, and every one of the 931 industries meeting discharge standards.

metrics.label: Industrial wastewater generated
metrics.value: 19.681862 MLD (25.6746 MLD per the water-quality chapter - see conflicts)

metrics.label: Industries not meeting discharge standards
metrics.value: Nil, per the plan - all 931 reported compliant

openActions: Inspection, sampling and show-cause / closure directions per CPCB inspection policy - KSPCB - continuous

districtThemes.summary: Three continuous and two manual monitoring stations, all in Mysuru city; the plan reports every town compliant with ambient standards and names blast furnaces, boilers, quarrying and stone crushing as the prominent sources.
openActions: Inventory of air pollution sources and hotspots; six-monthly task-force AAQ review around mining areas; pave unpaved roads - District task force + Mines & Geology + KSPCB + PWD - 31-03-2023

districtThemes.summary: Kyanite, magnesite, steatite, feldspar, quartz, black granite and building stone across 9 mining leases plus 26 quarry licences (186.2 ha); no sand mining, and the plan reports no illegal mining identified.

metrics.label: Licensed operations
metrics.value: 9 mining + QL 26 (34 total per the plan's notation)

openActions: District task force to monitor environmental compliance of mining - Mines & Geology Dept - standing

districtThemes.summary: Only KSPCB holds noise meters (2 portable devices); no fixed ambient noise stations exist in the district - the plan's action is procurement by ULBs, police and traffic police.
openActions: ULBs, SHOs and traffic police to procure portable noise meters - 31-03-2023
Install or retrofit fixed ambient noise stations with the existing CAAQM - District administration + KSPCB + ULBs - 31-03-2023

ulbs.name: Nanjangud
ulbs.note: On the Kabini's CPCB polluted stretch (the plan's own list includes 'Nanjungud to Hejjige', p.48). The restoration accountability matrix below tracks this stretch.

themes.summary: The plan shows Nanjangud with more STP capacity than generation and no gap - on 50% UGD coverage.

ulbs.name: T. Narasipura
ulbs.note: At the Kabini-Cauvery confluence; hosts the CWC gauge-discharge-quality station on the Kabini.
conflicts: The plan lists an existing 5.5 MLD STP on p.57 and p.60, but its treatment-capacity table on p.59 shows TN Pura at 0 MLD.

metrics.label: Existing STP capacity
metrics.value: 5.5 MLD (but 0 in the p.59 table - see conflict)

themes.summary: No STP and no sewerage network; a faecal sludge treatment plant is approved but not built.

ulbs.name: Sargur
ulbs.note: The NWMP monitors the Kabini downstream of Sargur village.

themes.summary: No STP, no sewerage network, and no facility marked as planned in the STP-requirement table.

districts.name: Chamarajanagara

dep.label: District Environmental Plan, Chamarajanagar (revised 23-06-2021, 71 pp)
dep.note: Published via chamrajnagar.nic.in. The plan text itself carries no date or review-cadence statement; the revision date is from the district website.

districts.countsNote: The plan's water framing is entirely Cauvery-side (Cauvery, Suvarnavathi, Palar; polluted stretch Mullur to Sattegala bridge, Priority IV under NGT OA 673/2018). The Kabini is never mentioned, although 22.4% of the district lies in the Kabini sub-basin polygon.
conflicts: Total sewage is 18.87 MLD in the water-quality chapter (p.51) but the sewage chapter's own table totals 18.8 MLD with only 10.5 MLD reaching STPs (p.62).
Groundwater quality monitoring frequency is 'yearly twice' on p.53 but 'once in two years' on p.55.
Biomedical waste generation is printed as '146 TPD' in one table against '146.34 kg/day' elsewhere - the TPD is the plan's own typo.
Two plastic-waste action deadlines read 31-3-2021, earlier than the plan's stated June-2021 revision.

districtThemes.summary: Full ULB-wise inventory: collection and door-to-door reach all 109 urban wards, but only 55 wards report 100% source segregation, all 3 built sanitary landfills are non-functional, and 57,057 tonnes of legacy waste sit in 3 old dumpsites.

metrics.label: ULB solid waste
metrics.value: Chamarajanagar 34.05, Kollegal 21, Gundlupet 10.83, Hanur 6.0, Yelandur 3.5 TPD

metrics.label: Sanitary landfills
metrics.value: 3 built, all non-functional; Gundlupet and Yelandur have none

openActions: Achieve 100% segregation at source (awareness, penalties, colour-coded bins) - ULBs - 31-12-2021
Make existing sanitary landfills functional; establish SLF at Gundlupet - ULBs - 31-03-2023
Remediate legacy dumpsites per CPCB guidelines (DPR exists only for Chamarajanagar town, work not started) - ULBs - 31-03-2023

districtThemes.summary: The plan inventories the Cauvery (~88 km with Palar and Suvarnavathi), 1,074 lakes (survey in progress) and the Priority-IV Mullur-Sattegala polluted stretch with 6 monthly NWMP sampling points plus a real-time station at Sattegala bridge; lake water quality is not monitored and no district environmental monitoring cell exists.

metrics.label: Rivers
metrics.value: Cauvery with Palar and Suvarnavathi, ~88 km in Kollegal taluk

metrics.label: Polluted river stretch
metrics.value: Mullur to Sattegala bridge (~18 km), Priority IV, NGT OA 673/2018

metrics.label: Drains joining the Cauvery on the stretch
NWMP river monitoring
metrics.value: 6 sampling points Mullur to Barachukki, monthly; continuous real-time station at Sattegala bridge

openActions: Constitute an environmental monitoring cell; inventorise drains, canals, rivers, groundwater, ponds, lakes - Minor Irrigation + Groundwater Authority + CNNL + Zilla Panchayat + KSPCB - 31-03-2022
Lake owners to monitor water quality per CPCB frequency, reporting quarterly - 31-03-2022
Restoration action plan for the Mullur-Sattegala stretch - implementation stated to be in progress - 31-03-2022

districtThemes.summary: 18.87 MLD generated against 21.6 MLD installed STP capacity in three towns, but UGD networks are only 70-75% complete so roughly half the sewage never reaches the plants (10.5 MLD of 18.8 reaches STPs per the plan's own table); Kollegal's flows reach the Cauvery via a canal, and Hanur and Yelandur have no UGD or STP at all.

metrics.label: STPs
metrics.value: Chamarajanagar 9 MLD, Kollegal 9 MLD, Gundlupet 2.1 + 1.5 MLD

metrics.label: Towns with no UGD or STP
Treated/untreated sewage reaching rivers
metrics.value: Not estimated - Kollegal STP discharges to a canal that joins the Cauvery; untreated missing-link flows also reach the river

openActions: Intercept and divert the missing links bypassing STPs; complete UGD connections - LBs + KUWS&DB + KUIDFC - 31-03-2023
DPR for sewage channelization and STPs for Hanur and Yelandur - 31-03-2023
Install web cams and OCEMS in STPs - 31-03-2023

districtThemes.summary: A small industrial base: 91 operating industries (4 Red, 28 Orange, 57 Green, 2 White), 23 discharging 1.88 MLD, all treated in captive ETPs with no CETP; the plan reports every discharging industry meeting standards.
openActions: Inspection and enforcement per CPCB policy - KSPCB - continuous

districtThemes.summary: One CAAQM station (KHB Colony, Chamarajanagar) and one manual station at the KSPCB regional office; all towns reported compliant with ambient standards; prominent sources are quarrying, stone crushers, m-sand units and unpaved roads.
openActions: District air pollution action plan: plantation, green belts in mining areas, paving, phasing out 15-year-old vehicles - District administration + Social Forestry + RTO + PWD - 31-03-2022

districtThemes.summary: 92 licensed operations including one riverbed sand mine at Mullur village and black-granite and building-stone quarries covering 1.21% of the district; a task force is constituted and no illegal mining is reported.
openActions: Task-force monitoring of environmental compliance - Mines & Geology Dept - standing

districtThemes.summary: Only KSPCB's regional office holds noise meters (2 portable devices); no fixed ambient noise stations exist.
openActions: ULBs, SHOs and traffic police to procure portable noise meters - 31-03-2022
Install fixed ambient noise stations with the existing CAAQM - 31-12-2023

counts.label: Urban Local Bodies (per the plan's table headings)
counts.value: 4 - Madikeri CMC; Kushalnagar, Somwarpet and Virajpet Town Panchayats

districts.countsNote: Only 4.1% of Kodagu lies in the Kabini sub-basin polygon - the upper tributary fringe. The plan is a 15-page scanned table set; unlike the Mysuru and Chamarajanagar plans it carries no readable narrative chapters.
